entries.title: Intracranial Pressure Dynamics (ICP/Volume Relationship, Cerebral Blood Flow, ICP Measurement, Elevated ICP)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ICP/volume relationship, cerebral blood flow, ICP measurement, and elevated-ICP recognition underlie the appropriate management plan (resuscitation, imaging, ongoing surveillance) required by this TBI objective.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Elevated ICP is a key 'red flag' cause of headache that the headache objective requires the candidate to recognize.

testable_competencies.icp_recognition: Given a patient with signs of elevated ICP (Cushing's triad, papilledema, declining GCS), recognize the physiologic basis and initiate urgent assessment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Herniation syndrome recognition (pupillary findings, posturing, GCS decline) is core to diagnosing severity/complications of TBI and initiating an appropriate management plan.

testable_competencies.herniation_recognition: Given clinical findings (blown pupil, decorticate/decerebrate posturing, Cushing's triad), identify the herniation syndrome and its urgency.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Initial management of elevated ICP (head of bed, sedation, osmotic therapy, hyperventilation, drainage) is squarely within 'initiate an appropriate management plan' for TBI/raised ICP.

testable_competencies.icp_management: State the stepwise conservative-to-aggressive management of elevated ICP (positioning, normocarbia, osmotic diuresis, sedation, CSF drainage, decompressive craniectomy).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: IIH is a recognizable secondary headache red-flag cause (papilledema/visual changes in a young obese woman) directly matching Headache objective 39's enabling objective to recognize "symptoms and signs that indicate a need for urgent brain imaging and/or referral for specialized care"; same evidentiary pattern as SU-NS-07 (Hydrocephalus) and SU-NS-13 (Meningioma), both classified COMPONENT.

testable_competencies.iih_recognition: Recognize IIH as a cause of headache/papilledema/visual changes in a young obese woman and the need for neuroimaging plus LP opening pressure to diagnose.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hydrocephalus is a red-flag structural cause of headache requiring recognition and imaging.

testable_competencies.hydrocephalus_classification: Differentiate obstructive vs. non-obstructive hydrocephalus and recognize NPH's classic triad.

entries.title: Metastatic Brain Tumours and Adult Diffuse Gliomas

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Metastatic brain lesions and gliomas enter the differential of a patient presenting with focal neurologic deficits alongside stroke, requiring the candidate to distinguish structural mass lesions from vascular events.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Shares imaging-driven approach to an intracranial mass/lesion, though metastatic disease/glioma is not itself traumatic.

testable_competencies.brain_tumour_recognition: Recognize the presentation of a supratentorial mass lesion (progressive headache, new focal deficit, seizure) and the role of contrast MRI in distinguishing metastasis from primary glioma.

entries.title: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma

testable_competencies.cns_lymphoma: Recognize primary CNS lymphoma as a ring-enhancing-lesion differential in an immunocompromised patient.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Meningioma is a common incidental/symptomatic extra-axial mass causing headache and progressive focal signs, relevant to headache red-flag recognition.

testable_competencies.meningioma_recognition: Recognize meningioma as the most common benign extra-axial primary brain tumour and its typical presentation/imaging appearance.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Vestibular schwannoma presents with unilateral sensorineural hearing loss/tinnitus, which is within the Otolaryngology-mapped hearing loss objective's differential.

testable_competencies.cpa_lesion_recognition: Recognize unilateral hearing loss/tinnitus with cerebellopontine angle mass as vestibular schwannoma requiring MRI.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pituitary adenoma with suprasellar extension classically causes bitemporal hemianopia, a visual-field defect the candidate must recognize and localize.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Progressive pituitary mass effect can present as chronic/progressive visual field loss.

testable_competencies.pituitary_mass_effect: Recognize bitemporal hemianopia and headache as suggesting a pituitary mass and the indication for pituitary MRI and endocrine workup; the endocrine hypersecretion/hypopituitarism syndromes themselves are primarily Endocrinology-owned content.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Brain abscess enters the differential of a focal intracranial lesion with fever, relevant to diagnosing cause/severity/complications of an intracranial process.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cerebral abscess is a source of systemic infection/leukocytosis referenced in that objective's scope of life-threatening WBC-related conditions.

testable_competencies.abscess_recognition: Recognize fever + headache + focal deficit + ring-enhancing lesion as suggesting cerebral abscess requiring urgent imaging and neurosurgical/ID involvement.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Epidural hematoma is a classic traumatic intracranial hemorrhage requiring recognition of cause, severity, and initiation of urgent management (this is a textbook TBI presentation).

testable_competencies.edh_recognition: Recognize the lucid-interval presentation and biconvex/lentiform CT appearance of epidural hematoma as a neurosurgical emergency.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Subdural hematoma is a classic traumatic intracranial hemorrhage, especially in elderly/anticoagulated patients, central to TBI diagnosis and management.

testable_competencies.sdh_recognition: Recognize the crescentic CT appearance of subdural hematoma and the higher-risk populations (elderly, anticoagulated, alcohol use) presenting subacutely/chronically.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Subarachnoid hemorrhage is a stroke subtype the candidate must diagnose (thunderclap headache) and manage urgently.

testable_competencies.sah_recognition: Recognize thunderclap headache as SAH until proven otherwise, and the urgent NCCT +/- LP (xanthochromia) diagnostic pathway.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Aneurysm is the leading cause of SAH; the stroke objective requires diagnosing severity/complications, which includes recognizing an unruptured/ruptured aneurysm on imaging.

testable_competencies.aneurysm_recognition: Recognize intracranial aneurysm as the cause of SAH and the basic surgical/endovascular options (clipping vs. coiling) without requiring technique-level detail.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Intracerebral hemorrhage is a stroke subtype requiring diagnosis of cause/severity/complications and initiation of management, including recognizing surgical decompression indications.

testable_competencies.ich_recognition: Recognize intracerebral hemorrhage on NCCT and the indications for urgent neurosurgical consultation (deterioration, mass effect, cerebellar hemorrhage).

entries.title: Arteriovenous Malformations, Cavernous Malformations, and Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 41 (stroke)'s own causal_conditions list explicitly names "Hemorrhage - Intracerebral and cerebellar - Subarachnoid" as a covered category; AVMs/cavernomas/dural AVFs are a canonical cause of exactly these hemorrhage subtypes in young/atypical patients, making this a direct rather than merely topic-adjacent match.

testable_competencies.vascular_malformation_recognition: Recognize vascular malformations as a cause of hemorrhage or seizure in a young patient without typical vascular risk factors.

entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: MODERATE MCC evidence retained even though classification stays SPECIALIST_DETAIL: objective 41's causal_conditions explicitly cover intracerebral/subarachnoid hemorrhage (the presentation these vascular malformations cause), giving genuine recognition-level relevance, but definitive management (embolization/surgery) remains specialist-level technique, so classification is unchanged from SPECIALIST_DETAIL.

testable_competencies.csf_fistula: Recognize CSF rhinorrhea/otorrhea after trauma as a possible CSF fistula requiring precautions against meningitis.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Back pain and related symptoms (e.g., sciatica)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cervical disc syndrome directly presents as neck pain with radicular features, matching this objective's determination of urgent vs. non-urgent intervention.

testable_competencies.cervical_radiculopathy: Recognize dermatomal/myotomal patterns of cervical nerve root compression and distinguish urgent (myelopathy) from non-urgent presentations.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Degenerative cervical myelopathy is a structural (UMN) cause of progressive weakness/gait change that this objective requires the candidate to localize and characterize.

testable_competencies.dcm_recognition: Recognize progressive gait disturbance, hand clumsiness, and UMN signs in an older patient as possible degenerative cervical myelopathy requiring MRI and surgical referral.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Back pain and related symptoms (e.g., sciatica)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Lumbar disc herniation with radiculopathy/sciatica is the prototypical instance of this back pain objective.

testable_competencies.lumbar_disc_recognition: Recognize sciatica from lumbar disc herniation and the indications for imaging vs. conservative management.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Back pain and related symptoms (e.g., sciatica)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cauda equina syndrome is the classic 'red flag' surgical emergency that the back pain objective requires the candidate to identify and act on urgently.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: New urinary retention/incontinence with saddle anesthesia is a cardinal cauda equina finding overlapping this objective's differential.

testable_competencies.ces_recognition: Recognize saddle anesthesia, bowel/bladder dysfunction, and bilateral leg weakness as cauda equina syndrome requiring emergent MRI and surgical decompression.

entries.title: Lumbar Spinal Stenosis and Neurogenic Claudication

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Back pain and related symptoms (e.g., sciatica)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

testable_competencies.stenosis_claudication: Differentiate neurogenic claudication (relief with flexion/sitting) from vascular claudication in an older patient with back and leg pain.
